stem: A 24-year-old man notices patches on his upper back after a beach holiday. They do not itch or hurt. A photograph of his back is shown.
oneliner: 24M + painless, non-itchy patches on upper back after beach holiday + [photo] → which organism?
ask: Which organism most likely causes this?

whyNot.B: **Tinea corporis**: itchy ring with a raised scaly edge and clear centre
whyNot.C: **Moist skin folds**, red with satellite pustules
whyNot.D: **Impetigo**: honey-crusted sores, often on the face
whyNot.E: **Secondary syphilis**: copper-coloured rash including palms and soles, with fever and lymph nodes

why: **Pale, fine-scaling patches that don't tan, appearing after sun and sweat on the upper back** = tinea versicolor. Malassezia makes **azelaic acid**, which blocks melanin, so the patches stay pale.

image.prompt: Upper back of an adult man with many small round and merging hypopigmented (paler than surrounding tanned skin) macules with fine powdery scale, no redness

bug.name: Malassezia furfur
bug.lab: KOH prep: short hyphae + round yeast = 'spaghetti and meatballs'
bug.virulence: Lipid-loving; makes azelaic acid that blocks tyrosinase (less pigment)
bug.spread: Overgrowth of own flora with heat, sweat, oily skin
bug.causes: Tinea (pityriasis) versicolor; fungemia with IV lipid feeds
